The load address is `in_ptr0 + (y0 + 128*x2 + 4032000*y1)`: consecutive threads along the x-dimension (XBLOCK) access memory with a stride of 128 floats = 512 bytes, causing severely uncoalesced reads. L1 hit rate is 0% so every access goes to L2, which is saturated at 96.76%. The scheduler has 80.45% idle cycles due to L1TEX stall (58% of all stall cycles). The current XBLOCK=128, YBLOCK=8 tile is suboptimal: a larger YBLOCK increases the number of y-indices per tile, which share the same x-stride pattern and can be prefetched together. Adding @triton.autotune with multiple (XBLOCK, YBLOCK, num_warps, num_stages) configurations will let the runtime find the tile shape that best hides memory latency and maximizes L2 reuse for this access pattern.
